+//! The verdict palette table (#1120): the colours that carry meaning -
+//! the Deviate verdict classes, the move kinds, the selection lift, the
+//! boundary roles and the warning / error / missing text inks - for each
+//! colour-vision mode, on a dark and on a light viewport. They are part
+//! of the token table, but they stay ours: no theme-file key sets them,
+//! because each set is held to the CIEDE2000 gate of `colorvision`.
+//! Values moved unchanged out of `colorvision.rs` and `ground_ink.rs`;
+//! `theme_files::verdict_inks` pins each one.
+//! Provenance: our own palette numbers (M13.4, #698); no vendor material
+//! consulted.
+
+use egui::Color32;
+
+use crate::egui_app::colorvision::{Semantic, TextInks};
+
+impl TextInks {
+    /// The house inks, exactly what the pages drew before: egui's own
+    /// dark-visuals warning (the theme builds on `Visuals::dark()` and
+    /// never respells it), the page red and the chip grey.
+    pub const HOUSE: TextInks = TextInks {
+        warn: Color32::from_rgb(255, 143, 0),
+        error: Color32::from_rgb(0xFF, 0x59, 0x59),
+        missing: Color32::from_rgb(0xB8, 0xB8, 0xC8),
+    };
+}
+
+impl Semantic {
+    /// The house palette, exactly what the shell drew before M13.4
+    /// (the overlay's own consts and the shaders' literals).
+    pub const OFF: Semantic = Semantic {
+        clean: [0.42, 0.50, 0.62],
+        rest: [0.98, 0.72, 0.20],
+        gouge: [0.90, 0.18, 0.14],
+        unjudged: [0.45, 0.46, 0.48],
+        feed: crate::interact::FEED_RGB,
+        rapid: crate::interact::RAPID_RGB,
+        plunge: crate::interact::PLUNGE_RGB,
+        select_hot: [0.98, 0.72, 0.20],
+        select_warm: [0.55, 0.35, 0.05],
+        bound_include: [0.20, 0.75, 0.95],
+        bound_exclude: [0.92, 0.25, 0.60],
+        bound_open: [0.98, 0.62, 0.12],
+        text_dark: TextInks::HOUSE,
+        text_light: TextInks::HOUSE,
+    };
+
+    /// Protan and deutan share the red-green confusion line, so one
+    /// remap serves both (each is still gated under its own eye):
+    /// rest goes lemon, gouge a dark oxblood, feed yellow against the
+    /// unchanged blue rapid, plunge a dark burnt orange - lightness
+    /// does the work the lost red-green axis did - and the unjudged
+    /// grey lifts clear of the steel.
+    pub const RED_GREEN: Semantic = Semantic {
+        clean: [0.42, 0.50, 0.62],
+        rest: [0.98, 0.85, 0.20],
+        gouge: [0.75, 0.10, 0.10],
+        unjudged: [0.80, 0.80, 0.80],
+        feed: [0.95, 0.85, 0.25],
+        rapid: [0.30, 0.50, 0.95],
+        plunge: [0.75, 0.30, 0.00],
+        select_hot: [0.98, 0.85, 0.20],
+        select_warm: [0.55, 0.48, 0.10],
+        bound_include: [0.25, 0.45, 1.00],
+        bound_exclude: [0.95, 0.90, 0.30],
+        bound_open: [0.95, 0.95, 0.95],
+        // Warning on the yellow end, refusal on the violet end of the
+        // surviving blue-yellow axis; the missing chip reads as a warning.
+        text_dark: TextInks {
+            warn: Color32::from_rgb(255, 230, 51),
+            error: Color32::from_rgb(204, 140, 255),
+            missing: Color32::from_rgb(255, 230, 51),
+        },
+        text_light: TextInks {
+            warn: Color32::from_rgb(140, 77, 0),
+            error: Color32::from_rgb(140, 0, 217),
+            missing: Color32::from_rgb(140, 77, 0),
+        },
+    };
+
+    /// Tritan loses blue-yellow: rest moves to pink (red-cyan survives),
+    /// gouge to a deeper red, rapid to a dark slate so lightness parts
+    /// it from the green feed.
+    pub const TRITAN: Semantic = Semantic {
+        clean: [0.42, 0.50, 0.62],
+        rest: [1.00, 0.45, 0.70],
+        gouge: [0.80, 0.05, 0.05],
+        unjudged: [0.80, 0.80, 0.80],
+        feed: crate::interact::FEED_RGB,
+        rapid: [0.20, 0.40, 0.60],
+        plunge: crate::interact::PLUNGE_RGB,
+        select_hot: [1.00, 0.45, 0.70],
+        select_warm: [0.56, 0.25, 0.40],
+        bound_include: [0.10, 0.70, 0.75],
+        bound_exclude: [0.90, 0.15, 0.20],
+        bound_open: [0.95, 0.95, 0.95],
+        // Red-cyan survives: warning goes cyan, refusal stays red.
+        text_dark: TextInks {
+            warn: Color32::from_rgb(77, 217, 217),
+            error: Color32::from_rgb(255, 128, 128),
+            missing: Color32::from_rgb(77, 217, 217),
+        },
+        text_light: TextInks {
+            warn: Color32::from_rgb(0, 107, 107),
+            error: Color32::from_rgb(179, 0, 26),
+            missing: Color32::from_rgb(0, 107, 107),
+        },
+    };
+
+    /// The house palette on a light viewport: the move kinds and the
+    /// boundary roles as tuned on screen (#698). Verdict and selection
+    /// inks are unchanged: they paint the stock and the selected part,
+    /// not lines on the ground.
+    pub const OFF_LIGHT_GROUND: Semantic = Semantic {
+        feed: [0.08, 0.36, 0.12],
+        rapid: [0.01, 0.31, 0.90],
+        plunge: [0.90, 0.13, 0.13],
+        bound_include: [0.10, 0.80, 1.00],
+        bound_exclude: [1.00, 0.20, 0.70],
+        bound_open: [1.00, 0.65, 0.05],
+        ..Semantic::OFF
+    };
+
+    /// Protan/deutan on a light viewport: the same blue-yellow axis as
+    /// `RED_GREEN`, darkened to clear 3:1 - gold feed and exclude against
+    /// the blue rapid and include; plunge and open go near-black, the
+    /// lightness end the dark ground's white open and pale inks held.
+    pub const RED_GREEN_LIGHT_GROUND: Semantic = Semantic {
+        feed: [0.55, 0.42, 0.00],
+        rapid: [0.01, 0.31, 0.90],
+        plunge: [0.22, 0.08, 0.00],
+        bound_include: [0.00, 0.30, 0.85],
+        bound_exclude: [0.55, 0.42, 0.00],
+        bound_open: [0.12, 0.12, 0.12],
+        ..Semantic::RED_GREEN
+    };
+
+    /// Tritan on a light viewport: red-cyan survives - the deep green
+    /// feed, red plunge and exclude, a teal include; rapid and open go
+    /// near-black so lightness parts them from the green.
+    pub const TRITAN_LIGHT_GROUND: Semantic = Semantic {
+        feed: [0.08, 0.36, 0.12],
+        rapid: [0.05, 0.05, 0.12],
+        plunge: [0.90, 0.13, 0.13],
+        bound_include: [0.00, 0.40, 0.45],
+        bound_exclude: [0.80, 0.05, 0.10],
+        bound_open: [0.12, 0.12, 0.12],
+        ..Semantic::TRITAN
+    };
+}

+//! keeps the colour the draw site wrote as a literal before, a theme

+use egui::Color32;
+
+/// The tool drawing inks of a token table, in the order of `KEYS`.
+fn inks(t: &Tokens) -> [Color32; 18] {
+    [
+        t.tool_ground,
+        t.tool_axis,
+        t.tool_grid,
+        t.tool_flute,
+        t.tool_shank,
+        t.tool_body,
+        t.tool_edge,
+        t.tool_holder,
+        t.tool_note,
+        t.tool_dim,
+        t.thumb_flute,
+        t.bad_ink,
+        t.warn_ink,
+        t.mount_axis,
+        t.mount_radial,
+        t.mount_tip,
+        t.mount_origin,
+        t.mount_hint,
+    ]
+}
+
+const KEYS: [&str; 18] = [
+    "tool_ground",
+    "tool_axis",
+    "tool_grid",
+    "tool_flute",
+    "tool_shank",
+    "tool_body",
+    "tool_edge",
+    "tool_holder",
+    "tool_note",
+    "tool_dim",
+    "thumb_flute",
+    "bad_ink",
+    "warn_ink",
+    "mount_axis",
+    "mount_radial",
+    "mount_tip",
+    "mount_origin",
+    "mount_hint",
+];
+
+fn parse(colors: &str) -> Tokens {
+    let text = format!(
+        r#"{{"format":"camcraft-theme/1","descriptor":{{"name":"t"}},"base":"dark","colors":{{{colors}}}}}"#
+    );
+    let theme = tf::parse_text(&text, "t.json").unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("the theme reads: {e}"));
+    assert!(theme.notes.is_empty(), "notes: {:?}", theme.notes);
+    theme.tokens
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn the_built_in_columns_keep_the_tool_drawing_colours() {
+    // The literals and consts of the tool pages, the tool library views
+    // and the tool body page before #1120. The previews draw on their own
+    // dark ground, so both columns hold the same set.
+    let before = [
+        Color32::from_rgb(24, 26, 31),
+        Color32::from_rgb(70, 74, 84),
+        Color32::from_rgb(80, 86, 98),
+        Color32::from_rgb(168, 178, 192),
+        Color32::from_rgb(122, 130, 142),
+        Color32::from_rgb(86, 92, 104),

+        Color32::from_rgb(90, 200, 230),
+        Color32::from_rgb(240, 180, 60),
+        Color32::from_rgb(240, 150, 40),
+        Color32::from_rgb(160, 160, 170),
+        Color32::from_rgb(240, 200, 120),

+}

+#[test]
+fn each_tool_drawing_ink_is_a_theme_key() {

+}

+## #1120 - The window chrome inks are tokens; the guard keeps only permanent rows
+
+**What was decided.**
+- Two colour tokens join `Tokens`, each also a theme-file key: `close_hover`
+  (the close button's hover fill, the desktop caption red `#C42B1C`) and
+  `close_ink` (the white cross on it). Both built-in columns keep the old
+  values. `window_chrome::CLOSE_HOVER` is gone; `caption` reads the tokens.
+- The `error_text.rs` row of the colour-literal guard was not a draw site.
+  Its one literal (`Color32::RED`) was in the file's inline test module,
+  and every caller passes a theme or palette ink. The test module moves to
+  `error_text_tests.rs`, which the guard skips as a test file.
+- The guard now has only `keep:` rows (the token tables, the verdict
+  palette table, the contrast maths and a colour that only measures text).
+- A new test pins the colour vocabulary inside the 64-entry map cap of a
+  theme file (61 keys now), as one already pins the geometry vocabulary.
+
+**Why.** These were the last Color32 literals at draw sites in
+`crates/ui/src`. A row that stays must have a reason that is not a theme
+choice.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- A light-column close red. The desktop caption red is the same on light
+  and dark title bars; a new value is a design change, not a move.
+- Teach the scanner to skip inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules. Only one file
+  had the case, and the sibling test file is the house pattern.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small: two fields and keys. The map cap has three
+free colour slots; a later family that needs more raises the cap.

+## #1120 - Tool drawing inks become theme tokens (fourth family)
+
+**What was decided.** Eighteen colour tokens join `Tokens`, each also a
+theme-file key (`colors.<name>`):
+- the tool, holder and profile previews: `tool_ground`, `tool_axis`,
+  `tool_grid`, `tool_flute`, `tool_shank`, `tool_body`, `tool_edge`,
+  `tool_holder`, `tool_note`, `tool_dim`;
+- the library thumbnails: `thumb_flute` (their shank reads `tool_shank`);
+- the refusal and warning inks of the tool pages: `bad_ink`, `warn_ink`;
+- the tool body page: `mount_axis`, `mount_radial`, `mount_tip`,
+  `mount_origin`, `mount_hint`.
+
+Both tables hold the old values, so no pixel changes. The previews draw on
+their own dark ground in the light theme too; that stays as it was.
+
+The module colour consts (`NOTE`, `BAD`, `HOLDER`, `BG`, ...) become small
+functions with the same visibility (`note_ink()`, `bad_ink()`,
+`holder_ink()`, `tool_ground()`, ...), which read the live token. Their
+callers change by name only.
+
+`theme::with_alpha(colour, alpha)` gives a token's own colour at an alpha.
+It reads the colour unmultiplied first, so a partly transparent token does
+not darken twice (the defect that the #3993 review found in the facet
+veil). The holder fills (alpha 90 in the profile, 70 in the preview) use
+it, and `ground_ink::facet_veil` now calls it too.
+
+**Why.** One key for each colour role, not one for each file: the same
+note grey was a const in five files, the axis line in three. `bad_ink` and
+`warn_ink` are general names, because the refusal red is also the text of a
+refused value on the cutter pages; the status family can reuse them.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- A light-column set for the previews. #1120 moves values; a light preview
+  ground is a separate design question.
+- Keeping the consts and adding the tokens beside them. Two sources for one
+  colour is what #1120 removes.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small: eighteen fields and keys; the functions
+keep the call sites stable.
+
+**Review of #4073: the drawing caches key on their inks.** The tool list
+thumbnails and the holder outline keep built shapes, and the shapes carry
+theme colours. Each cache key now holds the inks that its shapes carry
+(`thumb_flute` and `tool_shank`; `tool_axis`, `tool_body`, `tool_edge` and
+`tool_dim`). A theme change builds the drawing one time, and a still frame
+still builds nothing. Dropped: clearing the caches on a theme change. That
+needs a hook in the theme sync for each cache, and a key that holds its
+inputs is the frame-cost rule as `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` states it.

+## #1120 - The verdict palettes move into the token table, values unchanged
+
+**What was decided.** The six colour-vision palettes (`Semantic::OFF`,
+`RED_GREEN`, `TRITAN` and their `_LIGHT_GROUND` sets) and the house text
+inks (`TextInks::HOUSE`) move out of `colorvision.rs` and `ground_ink.rs`
+into a new table file, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme/verdict.rs`. The
+values do not change. The names do not change, so no call site changes:
+they are associated consts of `Semantic` and `TextInks`. `colorvision.rs`
+keeps the types, the CIEDE2000 gate and the simulation maths. The colour
+literal guard drops the `colorvision.rs` row and gets a `keep:` row for
+the new table. No theme-file key sets a verdict colour.
+
+**Why.** #1120 says it in the maintainer's words: "The verdict colours
+(gouge, rest, move kinds) and their colour-vision maths stay ours and stay
+as they are - they move into the token table, they do not change value."
+A theme key for them would let a file undo what the colour-vision gate
+proves for each mode.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- Theme keys for the house (Off) text inks only. The Off set is also the
+  base that the gate checks against the body text, and the same three
+  inks serve the dark and the light panel today. A key would need a
+  per-ground pair and a gate run at theme load. That is a separate design
+  question, not a move.
+- The palettes in `theme/tables.rs`. That file holds the two theme
+  columns (240 lines). A second table in it mixes a theme choice with a
+  fixed palette and pushes it toward the 400-line law.
+- Moving `interact::FEED_RGB`, `RAPID_RGB` and `PLUNGE_RGB` too. Other
+  code reads them as plain numbers (shaders, overlay lines). The Off
+  palette still names them, so they keep one source.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small: one file of consts. A theme key for a
+verdict colour later needs only the gate run at load, not a move.
